title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 32
paragraphs: So Aristagoras, hearing this, went back to Miletus greatly pleased; and meanwhile Artaphrenes, having sent to Susa and reported what Aristagoras had said, and Darius himself having joined in approving it, made ready two hundred triremes and a great host of Persians and their allies. He appointed as commander of these a Persian named Megabates, one of the Achaemenidae and cousin both to himself and to Darius—the same man to whose daughter Pausanias son of Cleombrotus the Lacedaemonian afterwards (if the story is true) became engaged, having conceived a desire to become tyrant of Hellas. Having appointed Megabates, I say, commander, Artaphrenes sent the armament off to Aristagoras.
